identity.name: Potassium phosphates
identity.chemical_class: Inorganic phosphate salts (potassium salts of phosphoric acid)

function.mechanism: Buffers and adjusts pH, complexes metal ions, supports water retention and structure in processed foods, and can support leavening systems.

adi.basis: Group ADI for phosphates, expressed as phosphorus (EFSA re-evaluation)

efsa.key_finding: EFSA re-evaluation set a group ADI of 40 mg/kg bw/day (as phosphorus) and identified ADI exceedance in younger populations, with concern for those with impaired renal function.

adi.basis: ADI not specified for monopotassium, dipotassium, and tripotassium phosphate entries

concerns.summary: Controlled feeding data indicate lowering phosphorus additive intake reduces urinary phosphorus, FGF23, and PTH, especially in CKD participants, supporting biologically meaningful mineral-metabolism effects.

Mechanistic and review evidence links rapidly absorbed inorganic phosphate additives to pathways relevant to vascular calcification and cardiorenal risk (FGF23/PTH axis), but causal long-term evidence specific to E340 in healthy populations is limited.
A recent mouse study reported anxiety-like behavior and neuroimmune changes after chronic high-phosphate feeding; human relevance remains uncertain.
One observational study suggested higher breast cancer risk at high phosphorus intake, but statistical uncertainty and design limitations prevent causal inference.

no_concern_confirmed: A single phosphate-enriched meal (700 mg phosphorus) did not significantly worsen postprandial inflammatory markers in healthy adults (PMID:38175251).

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported group ADI exceedance for younger populations and flagged renal-vulnerable groups as a concern.

risk_assessment.rationale: E340 remains approved/GRAS, but EFSA identified ADI exceedance in younger populations and uncertainty for vulnerable groups; human and mechanistic evidence indicates meaningful mineral-metabolism effects at relevant exposures.
key_factors: EFSA group ADI (40 mg/kg bw/day as phosphorus) with exceedance in youth
FDA GRAS status for dipotassium phosphate under GMP (21 CFR 182.6285)
JECFA entries report ADI not specified for potassium phosphate salts
No IARC listing/classification found for potassium phosphates
Intervention evidence shows additive phosphorus reduction changes FGF23/PTH markers
